structure.title: Derivatives
structure.heading: Note 14. Derivatives
structure.start_phrase: The Company uses interest rate swaps, currency swaps, and forward and option contracts to manage risks generally associated with foreign exchange rate and interest rate fluctuations.
structure.summary:
- Pension plan assets: Absolute return category includes hedge funds, insurance contracts, derivatives, hedge fund of funds, and other alternatives. Insurance contracts are valued at cash surrender value. Derivative instruments within plan assets (swaps, bond futures) are used for risk management. Other reconciling items include interest receivables/payables and amounts due for securities sold/purchased. Level 3 assets of international pension plans are primarily insurance contracts; balances decreased by $66 million in 2022 (net purchases/unrealized gains and losses −$24 million; currency −$42 million) and by $51 million in 2021 (net purchases/unrealized gains −$7 million; currency −$44 million).

- Derivatives (Note 14): 3M uses interest rate swaps, currency swaps, and forward/option contracts to manage FX and interest rate risks. Related information appears in notes on OCI (Note 8), fair value (Note 15), and long-term debt (Note 12).

- Cash flow hedges: Gains/losses recorded in OCI and reclassified when hedged transactions affect earnings; excluded components go to current earnings. FX forwards/options hedge forecasted foreign-currency cash flows with hedge horizons up to 36 months; de-designation policy described. Interest rate cash flow hedges include forward-starting swaps and treasury rate locks tied to forecasted debt issuances; 2020 $500 million treasury locks resulted in an immaterial AOCI loss amortized over note lives; 2019 terminations produced a $143 million AOCI loss being amortized. As of 12/31/22, after-tax net unrealized loss in AOCI from cash flow hedges was $7 million, including a $94 million after-tax loss from interest rate hedges; about $68 million after-tax net unrealized gain expected to be reclassified within 12 months (offset by hedged items). Pretax OCI impacts from cash flow hedges: 2022 $159 million gain (FX), 2021 $108 million gain, 2020 $113 million loss (including $(2) million from interest rate contracts in 2020).

- Fair value hedges: Changes in derivatives and hedged items recognized in current earnings. History of interest rate swaps converting portions of fixed-rate debt to floating (Eurobond due 2021; U.S. notes issued 2015; additional swaps in 2017 and 2018; 2021 swaps totaling $800 million converting parts of 2049/2050 notes through mid-2028). A discontinued 2007 swap on a 2028 debenture leaves a remaining basis adjustment. At 12/31/22, carrying value of hedged liabilities was $903 million with a cumulative fair value hedge basis adjustment of $(98) million (versus $997 million and $(4) million in 2021).

- Net investment hedges: Use of euro-denominated debt and FX forwards to hedge investments in foreign subsidiaries; spot-rate changes go to cumulative translation within OCI. At 12/31/22, designated notional amounts were ~€150 million in forwards and €2.4 billion of long-term debt, maturing 2023–2031. Amounts excluded from effectiveness testing were not material. Pretax OCI (cumulative translation) impacts: 2022 $172 million gain, 2021 $304 million gain, 2020 $352 million loss.

- Derivatives not designated as hedges: Include de-designated cash flow hedges and FX contracts used to offset non-functional currency exposures (e.g., intercompany balances); gains/losses recorded in earnings; no trading intent.

- Income statement impacts: Reclassifications from AOCI for FX cash flow hedges to cost of sales were $107 million in 2022 (vs. $(38) million in 2021 and $80 million in 2020). Interest rate cash flow hedge amortization impacted other expense (income), net by $(9) million each in 2020–2022. Fair value hedges produced offsetting gains/losses in other expense (income), net (e.g., $94 million hedged items and $(94) million derivatives in 2022). Non-designated FX derivatives yielded $(76) million in cost of sales and $45 million in other expense (income), net in 2022.

- Derivative fair values and notionals (12/31/22): Total derivative assets $217 million and liabilities $142 million. Designated FX forwards/options notionals: $2,368 million current and $835 million long-term; designated interest rate contracts: $800 million. Non-designated FX contracts: $2,816 million. Derivatives are recorded in other current assets/liabilities or other assets/liabilities.

- Credit risk and offsetting: Counterparty credit exposure is monitored via approvals, limits, and major international banks; master netting arrangements used where possible. 3M presents derivatives on a gross basis; if offset under master netting, 2022 derivative assets would net to $177 million and liabilities to $102 million; no cash collateral received.

- Currency effects: Net FX transaction impacts, including hedges, increased pre-tax income by ~$127 million in 2022 and decreased it by ~$105 million in 2021 and ~$21 million in 2020.

- Fair value measurements (Note 15): Recurring fair value relates mainly to available-for-sale marketable securities and derivatives; valuation uses market and income approaches. Marketable securities are priced via multiple sources and a distribution-curve-based algorithm; U.S. Treasuries are Level 1; other marketable securities (excluding certain U.S. municipals) are Level 2. No material recurring fair value measurements for nonfinancial items in 2022–2021.

  - ~4,028 individual claimants pending at 12/31/22 (up slightly from 2021); historical trial outcomes summarized.

  - 2022 activity: Accrual increased $31 million; $67 million in payments; ending accrual $604 million (excluding Aearo), with estimation horizon approaching 2050; insurance receivable $4 million.
  - Aearo Technologies-related respirator matters moved into Aearo chapter 11 trust process; historical indemnity and allocation arrangements described.
- Environmental matters and PFAS
  - Regulatory landscape: Rapidly evolving U.S. federal and state, EU, and international regulation of PFAS (drinking water, emissions, waste, TRI/TSCA actions, potential CERCLA/RCRA listings).
  - Europe/Belgium (Zwijndrecht): Stringent discharge/emission measures; new permits and infraction reports; operational impacts; agreement with Flemish Government totaling €571 million for controls, remediation, farmer support, and Oosterweel Project; ~$500 million charge recorded in 1H22; multiple Belgian civil cases and possible Dutch claims.
  - U.S. federal: EPA PFAS Roadmap; new health advisories; movement toward national drinking water standards; proposed CERCLA hazardous substance listings for PFOA/PFOS; TSCA test orders; TRI expansions.
  - U.S. states: Varied PFAS standards and product restrictions (e.g., CA, CO, ME); litigation and rule challenges (NJ/NY/MI); firefighting PPE notification compliance reviews.
  - Alabama (Decatur) and related settlements: Multiple resolutions (e.g., West Morgan-East Lawrence $35M, City of Decatur/Utilities/Morgan County ~$99M, Guin WWSB $30M); ongoing negotiations with property owners; new suits (e.g., Colbert County).
  - State AG PFAS suits: Numerous statewide actions, many centralized in AFFF MDL; others proceeding in state courts (e.g., NJ, NH, VT, IL, CA).
  - Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) litigation: ~3,350 lawsuits (including public water systems and putative classes) centralized in the South Carolina MDL; first water provider bellwether (City of Stuart, FL) targeted for June 2023; mediation ongoing; additional refinery/industrial suits (e.g., Valero subsidiaries).
  - Other PFAS product/environment lawsuits: Broad docket across NY (Hoosick Falls/Petersburgh), MI (with Wolverine), AL/GA water utilities and subscriber classes, GA Summerville, AL Tuskegee, CA Corona/Sacramento, NC Pittsboro, DE metal plating, NJ water systems and individuals, SC textile site, MA/ME local contamination, and an Ohio putative class seeking nationwide medical panel (appeal pending).
  - Compliance and remediation programs: Decatur (TSCA consent order issues, NPDES corrections, ADEM interim consent order, grand jury subpoena), Cordova (groundwater management, SDWA consent order; PFAS treatment), Cottage Grove (MPCA actions, stormwater order; incinerator retired); ongoing EPA/State information requests; congressional inquiry cooperation.
  - Other environmental litigation: Lower Passaic River cost recovery/contribution case (New Jersey).
  - Environmental liabilities/insurance: 2022 increase of $659 million in PFAS-related “other environmental liabilities”; $479 million payments; ending “other environmental liabilities” $592 million; separate non-PFAS remediation accrual $29 million; insurance receivable $8 million.
- Product liability litigation
  - Combat Arms Earplugs (Aearo/3M)
    - Aearo Entities filed chapter 11 in July 2022 to establish a trust; 3M committed $1.0B (plus $0.2B expenses), with potential additional funding; Aearo deconsolidated; related balance sheet effects disclosed.
    - Federal MDL (N.D. Fla.) bellwether outcomes mixed; appeals pending; injunction/stay disputes and mediation updates; state cases in Minnesota proceeding toward trial; no additional liability recorded beyond the funding commitment due to inability to estimate probable losses.
  - Bair Hugger patient warming system
    - ~5,258 U.S. lawsuits and a Canadian putative class; Eighth Circuit reversed MDL-wide summary judgment for 3M; mediation ordered; one Missouri state trial defense verdict; Minnesota state cases previously dismissed and affirmed; Canadian action pending.
- Securities and shareholder litigation
  - 2019 securities class actions regarding PFAS disclosures transferred to Minnesota and dismissed; multiple derivative actions in state and federal court largely stayed or under motions to dismiss (hearing held January 2023).
- Federal False Claims Act/qui tam (KCI/Acelity V.A.C. Therapy)
  - One qui tam (Godecke) dismissed; the other (Hartpence) revived by Ninth Circuit in August 2022 and remanded; case in pre-trial stage.
- Compliance matter
  - Internal investigation into China-based marketing travel/funding/record-keeping under the FCPA; voluntary disclosure to DOJ/SEC; discussions on potential resolution ongoing.
- Leases (Note 17)
  - 2022 lease expense: operating $295M; finance lease amortization $15M and interest $2M; variable $135M; total $447M (down from $463M in 2021 and $471M in 2020); short-term lease and sublease activity immaterial.

nodes.title: 3M COMPANY 2016 LONG-TERM INCENTIVE PLAN PERFORMANCE SHARE AWARD AGREEMENT
nodes.heading: EXHIBIT 10.32
nodes.start_phrase: Pursuant to the 3M Company 2016 Long-Term Incentive Plan (as amended from time to time, the “ Plan ”), 3M Company (the “ Company ”) granted to the participant listed below (“ Participant ”) the performance shares described below (the “ Performance Shares ”).
nodes.summary:
- Document type: 3M Company 2016 Long-Term Incentive Plan – Performance Share Award Agreement (Exhibit 10.32), incorporating the Plan, a Vesting Appendix (Appendix A), and a country-specific Global Appendix (Appendix B).
- Award basics: Grant to a named Participant of a target number of Performance Shares tied to a defined Performance Period (January 1–December 31 of specified years). Actual shares earned depend on continued service and achievement of performance goals. Each earned Performance Share delivers one share upon vesting; no rights to shares before vesting.
- Vesting: Follows the Vesting Schedule in Appendix A. Except as provided by the Plan/Agreement/Administrator (and, if applicable, under formal severance arrangements), unvested awards are forfeited if service terminates before the last day of the Performance Period. No prorated vesting or compensation for lost vesting unless explicitly provided. Special carve‑outs (bracketed in the form) may apply for Qualifying Termination and Retirement, and for death or Disability.
- Forfeiture for misconduct: All Performance Shares (including any vested portion) are immediately forfeited upon a written determination of Misconduct by the Administrator or an authorized representative, regardless of whether this occurs before or after termination of service.
- Dividend Equivalents: Granted on each Performance Share for ordinary cash dividends declared after the Grant Date and before settlement/forfeiture/expiration. Credited (without interest) to a separate Dividend Equivalent Account and vest/forfeit in tandem with the related Performance Share.
- Acceptance and administration: Participant accepts electronically by clicking “ACCEPT,” acknowledges review/understanding of the Agreement and Plan, and agrees that Administrator decisions and interpretations are final, binding, and conclusive.
- Notes on bracketed terms: “Qualifying Termination” provisions may be included only for retention/special grants (not annual grants). “Retirement” provisions are included for annual grants (not retention/special grants).

nodes.title: AWARD; VESTING; FORFEITURE AND SETTLEMENT
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I. AWARD; VESTING; FORFEITURE AND SETTLEMENT
nodes.start_phrase: This Award is expressed in terms of a Target Number of Performance Shares as set forth above (the “ Target Number of Performance Shares ”).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes an award of Performance Shares expressed as a Target Number, with actual shares earned based on continued service and achievement of performance goals.
- Each earned Performance Share entitles the participant to receive one Share upon satisfaction of vesting and other conditions; no rights to Share distribution before vesting.
- Grants Dividend Equivalents on ordinary cash dividends declared after the grant date and before settlement/forfeiture/expiration, tracked in a non-interest-bearing bookkeeping account and credited on dividend payment dates in amounts equal to dividends on one Share.
- Performance Shares vest per a Vesting Schedule in a Vesting Appendix; absent specific exceptions by the Administrator, the Plan, or this Agreement (e.g., certain qualifying terminations, retirement, death, disability as applicable), unvested Performance Shares are canceled upon Termination of Service before the end of the performance period.
- No pro‑rata vesting or compensation for lost vesting if service ends before the performance period ends, except as provided in specified sections or under a formal written severance plan/agreement.
- Any act of Misconduct results in immediate forfeiture and cancellation of all Performance Shares (including any vested portion) upon a written determination by the Administrator or authorized representative, regardless of whether determined before or after termination.
- Dividend Equivalents vest and forfeit in tandem with their associated Performance Shares.
- Notes clarify that “Qualifying Termination” provisions may be included for retention/special grants (not annual grants) and “Retirement” provisions are included for annual grants (not retention/special grants).

nodes.title: Performance Shares and Dividend Equivalents.
nodes.heading: 1.1 Performance Shares and Dividend Equivalents .
nodes.start_phrase: This Award is expressed in terms of a Target Number of Performance Shares as set forth above (the “ Target Number of Performance Shares ”).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a Performance Share award defined by a Target Number of Performance Shares; actual shares earned depend on continued service and achievement of performance goals.
- Each earned Performance Share entitles the participant to one Share upon satisfaction of terms; no right to any Share distribution until vesting.
- Grants Dividend Equivalents on each Performance Share for ordinary cash dividends declared after the Grant Date and before the Performance Share is settled, forfeited, or expires.
- Dividend Equivalents are credited (without interest) to a separate Dividend Equivalent Account in an amount equal to dividends on one Share and vest/forfeit in tandem with the related Performance Share.
- Vesting follows a Vesting Schedule set forth in a Vesting Appendix, subject to Administrator discretion and the Plan/Agreement.
- If Termination of Service occurs before the end of the Performance Period, unvested Performance Shares are immediately forfeited, except as otherwise provided (including potential exceptions for Qualifying Termination, Retirement, death, Disability, or under specific sections/plan terms).
- No prorated vesting or compensation for lost vesting if service ends before the Performance Period concludes, unless expressly provided.
- Any Misconduct (as determined in writing by the Administrator or authorized representative) triggers immediate forfeiture of all Performance Shares, including any vested portion.
- Notes clarify that Qualifying Termination provisions may apply only to retention/special grants, and Retirement provisions may apply only to annual grants.

nodes.title: Vesting; Forfeiture
nodes.heading: 1.2 Vesting; Forfeiture
nodes.start_phrase: The Performance Shares will vest according to the vesting schedule set forth in the Vesting Appendix (the “ Vesting Schedule ”).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes an award of Performance Shares expressed as a Target Number; actual shares earned depend on continued service and achievement of performance goals.
- Each earned Performance Share delivers one Share upon vesting; no right to any Share distribution before vesting.
- Grants Dividend Equivalents on ordinary cash dividends declared after the grant date and before settlement/forfeiture/expiration; amounts are credited without interest to a separate bookkeeping account for each Performance Share.
- Vesting follows a Vesting Schedule in a Vesting Appendix; absent specific exceptions by the Administrator, the Plan, this Agreement, or a written severance plan:
  - Unvested Performance Shares are forfeited if service terminates before the end of the performance period, subject to possible exceptions for a Qualifying Termination, Retirement, death, or Disability (as applicable).
  - No pro‑rated vesting or compensation for lost vesting if service ends before the performance period ends, except as set out in Sections 1.3 and 1.5 or a formal severance arrangement.
- All Performance Shares, including any vested portion, are immediately forfeited upon a written determination that the participant engaged in Misconduct, regardless of whether that determination occurs before or after termination of service.
- Dividend Equivalents vest or are forfeited in tandem with the related Performance Shares.
- Notes clarify that “Qualifying Termination” provisions may be included only for retention/special grants (not annual grants), and “Retirement” provisions are included for annual grants (not retention/special grants).

nodes.title: Special Vesting Provisions.
nodes.heading: 1.3 Special Vesting Provisions .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 1.2 or the Vesting Schedule, the Performance Shares shall continue to vest, or vest on an accelerated basis, in the event of Participant’s Termination of Service prior to the last day of the Performance Period under the following circumstances:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes special vesting rules that override the standard vesting schedule when a participant’s service ends before the performance period ends.
- Qualifying Termination or Retirement:
  - Performance Shares continue to vest on the original schedule as if service had continued, subject to potential accelerated vesting under clause (c).
  - May require timely execution and non-revocation of a company-prescribed general release (excluding indemnification/D&O coverage).
  - Target shares are prorated as of termination:
    - Appointed to the Executive Conference between Jan 1, 2006 and Dec 31, 2017: prorated by whole months of service during the performance period divided by total months in the period.
    - Appointed before Jan 1, 2006 or after Dec 31, 2017: prorated by completed three-month periods served during the first 12 months of the performance period divided by four.
  - Company may withhold favorable Retirement treatment if counsel advises it would be unlawful/discriminatory, in which case standard non-Retirement rules apply.
- Disability:
  - Performance Shares continue to vest per the original schedule as if service had continued, subject to potential accelerated vesting under clause (c).
- Death:
  - If death occurs before the period ends, or after a Qualifying Termination/Retirement/Disability, vesting accelerates to the lesser of the target number of shares or another number determined at the Administrator’s discretion.
- “Disability” is defined by U.S. Treasury Regulation section 1.409A-3(i)(4).

nodes.title: Settlement.
nodes.heading: 1.4 Settlement .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Except as provided in Section 1.4(c), all of Participant’s Performance Shares which are then vested will be paid in Shares, and any related Dividend Equivalents (including any Dividend Equivalent Account balance) will be paid in cash, in each case, during the thirty (30)-day period beginning with the earliest to occur of the following events:
nodes.summary:
- Vested Performance Shares are settled in Company Shares; related Dividend Equivalents (including any account balance) are paid in cash.
- Payment occurs within a 30-day window starting on the earliest of: (i) the Certification Date (and in any case no later than March 15 of the year following the Performance Period for this trigger), (ii) the participant’s death, or (iii) the participant’s Termination of Service following a Change in Control (with a 409A “separation from service” requirement if the participant is or becomes Retirement-eligible).
- To comply with Section 409A, distributions triggered by separation from service may be delayed for six months if required (e.g., for specified employees); delayed amounts are paid in a 30-day window after the six-month period or earlier if permitted (such as upon death).
- Section 1.4(b) is reserved.
- Participants may elect to defer the timing of Share delivery if the Company permits, by making a timely, valid election on a Company-approved form, in full compliance with Section 409A, Treasury Regulations, and Plan rules; approved deferral elections are incorporated by reference.
- Distribution timing cannot be altered except as allowed by the Administrator in compliance with Section 409A.
- Change in Control protection: If, within 18 months after a Change in Control and before the end of the Performance Period, the participant is terminated by the Company/Subsidiary other than for Misconduct or resigns for Good Reason, the participant vests in a calculated number of Performance Shares (specific formula continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Effect of Change in Control.
nodes.heading: 1.5 Effect of Change in Control .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Vesting Schedule or Sections 1.2 and 1.3, in the event of Participant’s Termination of Service prior to the last day of the Performance Period (i) by the Company or any Subsidiary other than as a result of Participant’s Misconduct or (ii) by Participant for Good Reason, in either case, within eighteen (18) months following a Change in Control of the Company, Participant shall vest in a number of Performance Shares equal to the sum of:
nodes.summary:
- Settlement of awards:
  - Vested Performance Shares are paid in Shares; related Dividend Equivalents (including any Dividend Equivalent Account) are paid in cash.
  - Payment occurs within 30 days of the earliest of: (i) the Certification Date (and in all cases no later than March 15 of the year following the Performance Period), (ii) the participant’s death, or (iii) the participant’s Termination of Service following a Change in Control (with an added requirement that, if the participant is or will be Retirement-eligible during the Performance Period, the termination must be a “separation from service” under Section 409A).
  - If payment would violate Section 409A’s six‑month delay rule for specified employees, distributions are delayed and paid in the 30‑day period after the delay ends (or earlier upon death) without violating 409A.
  - Section 1.4(b) is reserved.
  - Company‑permitted deferral elections may change timing of Share delivery if made on approved forms and compliant with Section 409A and Plan rules; otherwise, distribution timing cannot be changed except as allowed by the Administrator under 409A.

- Effect of Change in Control:
  - If, within 18 months after a Change in Control and before the end of the Performance Period, the participant is terminated by the Company (other than for Misconduct) or resigns for Good Reason, vesting accelerates to:
    - Completed calendar years: the Vesting Eligible Shares determined under the Vesting Schedule; plus
    - Incomplete calendar years: the greatest of (i) vesting based on annualized actual performance through completed quarters in the year of termination, (ii) vesting based on the average actual annual performance for the most recent three consecutive completed calendar years, or (iii) such other number set by the Administrator.
  - The total is prorated based on full calendar months elapsed in the Performance Period before termination.
  - Good Reason means a material diminution in position/authority/duties, a material reduction in base salary or planned annual cash compensation, or a material change in required work location.

- Taxation and withholding:
  - The participant is ultimately responsible for all tax-related items arising from the award (income, social, payroll, fringe, etc.), which may exceed amounts withheld.
  - The Company/Employer make no tax advice or guarantees and may need to account for taxes in multiple jurisdictions.

nodes.start_phrase: Certain capitalized terms used but not defined in this Global Appendix have the meanings set forth in the Performance Share Award Agreement (the “ Agreement ”) or, if not defined therein, the Plan.
nodes.summary:

  - Advises participants to seek professional advice; information may not fit individual circumstances and may not apply if residency/citizenship differs or changes.

- Data privacy
  - EEA+ (EU/EEA/Switzerland/UK): Participants must review and accept a Data Privacy Notice and Declaration of Consent via the Company’s Fidelity platform to accept the Agreement.
  - Outside EEA+: Participant consents to collection, use, storage, and transfer of personal data among the Company, Employer, Subsidiaries, and service providers (notably Fidelity), including cross-border transfers (e.g., to the U.S.). Lists categories of personal data and purposes (plan administration).
  - Rights to view, correct, inquire about processing/storage, and to refuse/withdraw consent; refusal/withdrawal may preclude receipt or administration of awards. Company may request additional privacy acknowledgments to comply with local law.

- Country-specific terms and notifications (illustrative highlights)
  - Argentina: No public offer/listing; exchange controls and foreign asset reporting obligations.
  - Australia: Offer made under Corporations Act Division 1A; plan intended to qualify under Subdivision 83A-C; exchange control reporting thresholds.
  - Austria: Quarterly/annual reporting to National Bank for foreign securities and non-Austrian cash accounts over thresholds.
  - Belgium: Foreign asset/bank account reporting; stock exchange tax on sales via non-Belgian intermediaries; annual securities account tax above thresholds.
  - Brazil: Compliance with Brazilian laws and taxes; acknowledgment that share value may vary; exchange control declarations; IOF tax may apply on remittances.
  - Canada: Redefines “Termination Date” for vesting cessation; Quebec-specific privacy disclosures and possible profiling/automated decisioning; foreign property reporting (T1135); sales through exchanges outside Canada (e.g., NYSE).
  - Chile: Awards/shares not part of severance base; private offering under CMF NCG 336 (Spanish notice included); exchange control thresholds; annual tax reporting (Form 1929) and potential registration of share acquisitions.
  - China (SAFE-restricted participants): Forfeiture 6 months after termination; mandatory sale of shares on/after termination; strict tax withholding methods; mandatory repatriation of sale proceeds, dividends, and dividend equivalents to a SAFE-approved account with quarterly FX conversion limits; vesting/settlement contingent on valid SAFE approvals.
  - Colombia: Awards not salary; no public offer; exchange control registration and potential Central Bank reporting; annual foreign assets reporting.
  - Croatia: Vested awards settled in cash (Company may choose shares).
  - Czech Republic: Possible CNB notifications for foreign assets/accounts and investments above thresholds.
  - Denmark: Acknowledgment of amended Danish Stock Option Act and receipt of Danish Employer Statement; foreign asset/account reporting.
  - Ecuador: Net worth and foreign monetary asset reporting above thresholds.
  - France: Consent to English documents; French-Qualified Performance Shares under a French sub-plan with special tax/social regimes; minimum 2-year holding, closed-period sale restrictions, continued restrictions after termination (except death/disability), 20% holding for managing officers, in-life transfer prohibitions, death provisions for heirs; foreign asset/account reporting.
  - Germany: Monthly cross-border payment reporting to Bundesbank above thresholds; “qualified participation” reporting if ownership/value thresholds met.
  - Hong Kong: No sale within six months if vest within six months of grant; private offer warning—documents not a prospectus and for employees only.
  - India: Cash settlement (Company may choose shares); mandatory repatriation of proceeds/dividends/dividend equivalents with documentation; foreign asset/account reporting on tax return.
  - Indonesia: Language consent acknowledging English documents (Bahasa translation available); bank reporting for inbound transfers and participant transfer form; annual reporting of worldwide assets.
  - Additional countries covered (some with “no country-specific terms”): Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica (none), Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic (none), Ecuador, El Salvador (none), Finland (none), France, Germany, Greece (none), Guatemala (none), Hong Kong, Hungary (none), India, Indonesia, Ireland (none).

- Common themes across jurisdictions
  - Securities law status (often private offers; not publicly listed/registered locally).
  - Exchange control rules, reporting, approvals, and repatriation duties.
  - Tax reporting of foreign assets/accounts and transaction proceeds.
  - Employment/labor law acknowledgments clarifying awards are not salary or severance components.
  - Special vesting, settlement, termination, and sale restrictions tailored to local law.

nodes.title: APPENDIX A TO STOCK OPTION AWARD AGREEMENT
nodes.heading: APPENDIX A TO STOCK OPTION AWARD AGREEMENT

nodes.heading: DATA PRIVACY PROVISIONS APPLICABLE TO PARTICIPANTS OUTSIDE THE EEA+

Participants can request recipient lists, access and correct data, and withdraw consent via local HR. Consent is voluntary, but refusal/withdrawal may prevent grant or administration of awards (without affecting employment). The company may later rely on different legal bases or require additional consents; failure to provide required consents may bar plan participation.

Regulations change frequently—participants should consult personal legal advisors and comply with all currency restrictions, approvals, and reporting.

nodes.title: AUSTRALIA
nodes.heading: AUSTRALIA
nodes.start_phrase: This offer is being made under Division 1A of Part 7.12 of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) (“Division 1A”).
nodes.summary:
- Offer made under Division 1A of Part 7.12 of Australia’s Corporations Act; this document is an ESS Offer Document. Information is general only and not personal financial advice; participants should seek their own advice and monitor risks.
- Additional Documents provided: the Plan, Plan Prospectus (not a Corporations Act prospectus), Agreement, and a Tax Summary. Participants should rely only on these written materials.
- Risk factors: Share price may fluctuate due to market conditions, economic and regulatory changes, and company-specific risks; further details in the company’s latest Form 10-K/10-Q. USD/AUD exchange rate movements affect Share value and Option exercise cost.
- Common stock overview: U.S. common stock analogous to Australian ordinary shares; one vote per share; dividends at Board discretion; traded on NYSE under “MMM”; no further capital calls, pre-emptive, conversion, redemption, or sinking fund rights.
- Market price information: Current/historical prices available on NYSE website (symbol MMM); AUD equivalents via Reserve Bank of Australia exchange rates.
- Grant and exercise price: No cost to receive the Option; exercise price set by the company at not less than fair market value on grant date; price is in USD and must be paid in USD; AUD amount varies with exchange rates.
- Division 1A statutory terms:
  - Application period: Participant may not accept or acquire the Option until at least 14 days after receiving the ESS Offer Document; acceptance allowed any time thereafter during the Option’s life.
  - Disclosure requirements: Documents must not be misleading or deceptive and must be updated if materially out of date or incorrect; designated persons must notify the company of issues during the application period; participants may recover losses for contraventions per specified rules.
  - Liability exclusions: No liability where reasonable inquiries were made and beliefs were reasonable, lack of knowledge, reasonable reliance on third-party information, public withdrawal of consent to be named, or new circumstances unknown to the person.
- Australia notifications:
  - Tax: Plan intended to be subject to Subdivision 83A-C of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (subject to conditions).
  - Exchange control: Reporting may be required for certain cash and international fund transfers; an Australian bank may report on the participant’s behalf; otherwise the participant must. Seek personal advice for compliance.
- Austria notifications:
  - Exchange control: Possible obligation to file annual reports to the Austrian National Bank for securities held abroad (form Standmeldung/Wertpapiere) if thresholds are met; quarterly valuation and filing deadlines apply.
  - Foreign cash accounts: Additional reporting for cash held abroad when selling shares or receiving dividends; monthly reports required if transaction volumes exceed thresholds (form Meldungen SI-Forderungen und/oder SI-Verpflichtungen).

nodes.title: AUSTRIA

nodes.title: BELGIUM
nodes.heading: BELGIUM
nodes.start_phrase: If Participant wishes to accept the Option, Participant must do so within 60 days after the date the Agreement and other grant materials related to the Option are published on Fidelity's website and made available to Participant (the “Offer Date”).
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Country-specific terms for stock option grants under a company plan, covering Belgium and Brazil.

- Belgium
  - Acceptance window: Must accept the option within 60 days of the communicated Offer Date (materials posted on Fidelity). No action within 60 days = deemed rejection and cancellation.
  - Restriction: Participant may not enter into an undertaking not to exercise or transfer the option before the end of the third full calendar following the year of the Offer Date.
  - Reporting and taxes:
    - Foreign assets/accounts: Belgian residents must report foreign securities and bank accounts on the annual tax return and separately report foreign account details to the National Bank of Belgium (forms on NBB website).
    - Stock exchange tax: May apply to transactions executed via non-Belgian intermediaries (e.g., U.S. broker), including sales of plan shares.
    - Annual securities account tax: Annual tax may apply if the total value in securities accounts exceeds a threshold on the reference dates (Dec 31, Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 30); obligations differ for Belgian vs. foreign institutions; consult a tax advisor.

- Brazil
  - Compliance: Participant agrees to comply with Brazilian law and is responsible for taxes related to option exercise, dividends, and sale of shares.
  - Labor law acknowledgment: Participation is an investment decision; share value is variable and not guaranteed.
  - Exchange control: Brazilian residents must file annual or quarterly declarations with the Central Bank of Brazil for foreign assets/rights if they exceed specified thresholds.

nodes.title: BRAZIL
nodes.heading: BRAZIL
nodes.start_phrase: By accepting the Option, Participant acknowledges and agrees to comply with applicable Brazilian laws and to pay any and all applicable Tax-Related Items associated with the exercise of the Option, the receipt of any dividends, and the sale of the Shares acquired under the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: Country-specific terms and notifications for participation in a stock option plan covering Belgium, Brazil, and Canada.

- Belgium
  - Acceptance window: Participant must accept the option within 60 days from the Offer Date (as posted on Fidelity and separately communicated). Failure to act within 60 days cancels the option; inaction is deemed rejection.
  - Restriction: Participant is not permitted to enter into an undertaking not to exercise or transfer the option before the end of the third full calendar year following the year of the Offer Date.
  - Notifications:
    - Foreign asset/account reporting: Belgian residents must report foreign securities and accounts on the annual tax return and separately report account details to the National Bank of Belgium.
    - Stock exchange tax: May apply to transactions executed through a non-Belgian intermediary (e.g., sale of plan shares via a U.S. broker).
    - Annual securities account tax: Annual tax may apply if the total value of securities in Belgian or foreign accounts exceeds a threshold on four reference dates (Dec 31, Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 30); obligations vary by institution location. Tax advice recommended.

- Brazil
  - Compliance: Participant agrees to comply with Brazilian laws and pay all applicable taxes on option exercise, dividends, and share sales.
  - Labor law acknowledgment: Participation is an investment decision; share value can fluctuate without compensation.
  - Notifications:
    - Exchange control: Brazilian residents may need to file annual or quarterly declarations to the Central Bank if foreign assets/rights (including plan shares and possibly options) exceed thresholds.
    - IOF tax: Financial transactions related to foreign payments, repatriation, and BRL/USD conversions (including exercise price payments) may be subject to IOF; participant is responsible. Tax advice recommended.

- Canada
  - Termination of employment (replaces Agreement Subsection 3.1(l)):
    - Termination Date is the earliest of: (i) termination date, (ii) date notice is received, or (iii) date active services cease, regardless of reason or later legal findings.
    - Vesting ceases on the Termination Date; any post-termination exercise window (if applicable) starts then. Notice periods or pay in lieu do not extend the Termination Date. Administrator has discretion, including for leaves.
    - If employment standards legislation mandates vesting during statutory notice, vesting only continues through the end of the minimum statutory notice period; no pro‑rated vesting beyond, and no compensation for lost vesting.
  - Non-qualified securities: Some or all shares may be non-qualified securities under the Income Tax Act (Canada); the Company will provide required tax characterization notices/information.
  - Data privacy (Quebec): Authorization for the Company/Employer to obtain, record, and discuss plan-related information with personnel and advisors; personal (including sensitive) information may be transferred outside Quebec (including to the U.S.); acknowledgment of potential profiling and automated decisions by the Company, Employer, subsidiaries, and Fidelity.

nodes.title: CANADA
nodes.heading: CANADA
nodes.start_phrase: The following provision replaces Subsection 3.1(l) of the Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Country-specific provisions for an equity incentive/stock option plan covering Brazil, Canada, and Chile, including tax, employment, data privacy, payment/exercise mechanics, and securities/reporting obligations.

- Brazil:
  - Reporting: Rights to be reported may include Shares acquired and Options granted under the Plan.
  - Tax on Financial Transactions (IOF): Applies to foreign payments (including exercise price), repatriation of funds, and BRL/USD conversions related to the Plan. Participant is responsible for compliance and should seek tax advice.

- Canada:
  - Termination of Employment: “Termination Date” is the earliest of (i) actual termination, (ii) notice date, or (iii) the date active service ceases; vesting stops at the Termination Date; post-termination exercise window (if any) starts then. No extension for notice/pay in lieu. Admin has discretion, including for leaves. Statutory notice vesting only to end of minimum statutory notice; no pro‑rata vesting or compensation beyond that.
  - Non-Qualified Securities: Some or all Shares under the Option may be “non-qualified securities” under the Income Tax Act (Canada); Company will provide required tax characterization information.
  - Data Privacy (Quebec): Authorization for the Company/Employer to discuss, record, and store Plan-related information, including sensitive data; permits cross-border transfers (including to the U.S.); potential profiling/automated decisions by Company, Employer, Subsidiaries, and Fidelity.
  - Form of Payment: Canadian residents cannot use certain specified methods to pay the exercise price or Tax-Related Items as referenced in the Agreement.
  - Exercise Mechanics: Certain automatic exercise/settlement provisions do not apply; instead, any vested, outstanding portion immediately before term expiry (or applicable death window) will be cash-settled for the intrinsic value.
  - Securities Law: Shares may be sold through the Plan’s designated broker outside Canada via a listed exchange (e.g., NYSE).
  - Foreign Asset/Account Reporting: Form T1135 required if foreign specified property exceeds the threshold; includes Shares and may include Options (generally at nil cost). Share ACB generally equals FMV at acquisition and may need averaging. Filing generally due April 30; seek personal advice.

- Chile:
  - Labor Law Acknowledgment: Options/Shares and related income/value are not part of remuneration for purposes of severance or notice calculations under Article 172 of the Chilean Labor Code.
  - Securities Law: Private offering in Chile as of Grant Date under CMF General Ruling No. 336; Options/Shares not registered or supervised by the CMF; no obligation to provide public information; no public offering unless registered.

nodes.title: CHILE
nodes.heading: CHILE
nodes.start_phrase: The Option and any Shares acquired under the Plan, and the income and value of same, shall not be considered as part of Participant's remuneration for purposes of determining the calculation base of future indemnities, whether statutory or contractual, for years of service (severance) or in lieu of prior notice, pursuant to Article 172 of the Chilean Labor Code.
nodes.summary:
- Canada
  - Payment methods: Canadian residents cannot use certain methods to pay the exercise price or tax withholdings referenced in Agreement Sections 2.3(c), 2.3(d), and 2.4(c).

  - Foreign asset/account reporting: Possible T1135 filing if the total cost of foreign specified property exceeds the threshold; options typically reported at nil cost; share ACB generally FMV at acquisition and may need to be averaged with other holdings; filing due by April 30; consult a personal advisor.

  - Labor law: Options, shares, and related income/value are not part of remuneration for calculating statutory or contractual severance or notice in lieu under Article 172 of the Chilean Labor Code.
  - Securities law: Private offering under CMF General Rule No. 336; options and shares are not registered in Chile, are not subject to CMF oversight, and cannot be publicly offered in Chile unless registered. Spanish notice included.
  - Exchange controls: Possible reporting/approval requirements if remitting amounts over certain thresholds or if aggregate foreign investments exceed limits; rules may change; consult a local advisor.
  - Tax reporting/registration: Annual CIRS reporting of foreign investment results and foreign taxes via Form 1929 (due June 30). Optional registration of share purchases with the CIRS to evidence acquisition price; the company/administrator is not obligated to provide supporting reports; seek legal/tax advice.

- China (for participants subject to SAFE)
  - Forfeiture: Unexercised options are forfeited six months after termination of service (or earlier if required by SAFE), regardless of reason, unless previously exercised/expired/canceled.
  - Mandatory sale upon termination: Participants must promptly sell any shares acquired on exercise after termination (including retirement, death, or disability). If not sold in a reasonable time, the company may sell on the participant’s behalf at its discretion and without price obligations.

nodes.title: CHINA
nodes.heading: CHINA

nodes.summary:

Colombia:

- Exchange controls: Participant is responsible for complying with Colombian foreign exchange restrictions, approvals, and reporting related to the options, shares, and fund transfers.

nodes.title: COLOMBIA
nodes.heading: COLOMBIA

nodes.title: COSTA RICA

nodes.title: RUSSIA
nodes.heading: RUSSIA

nodes.title: SERBIA

- Thailand
  - Exchange controls for exercising options: Remitting funds abroad requires compliance with exchange control rules, including an application through an authorized commercial bank with a Foreign Exchange Transaction Form, a letter describing the option, plan documents, and proof of company–employer nexus. If exercising without remitting funds, this requirement does not apply.
  - Repatriation and conversion: Sale or dividend proceeds above a specified threshold must be immediately repatriated to Thailand; within 360 days, proceeds must be converted to Thai Baht or deposited into a foreign currency deposit account, unless an exemption applies (e.g., offshore use with proper filings).
  - Reporting and penalties: Inward remittances must be reported to the Bank of Thailand via a foreign exchange transaction form; noncompliance may result in penalties. Participants are responsible for compliance and should consult a personal legal advisor.

nodes.title: THAILAND

Notes a limitation for directors/executive officers under Exchange Act Section 13(k), where indemnification could be treated as a prohibited loan; in such cases, unpaid taxes may be treated as a taxable benefit, triggering additional income tax and employee National Insurance contributions (NICs). The participant must self-assess and pay income tax to HMRC and reimburse/pay employee NICs to the company/employer, recoverable as per Section 2.4 of the Agreement.

- Vietnam (Cash Settlement): Allows the company to restrict share delivery upon option exercise and instead require a cash payment equal to the option’s intrinsic value. - Post-termination rules: RSUs generally do not vest after Termination of Service, except as provided in Sections 1.3 and 1.5, the Appendix, or by the Administrator; no prorated vesting or compensation for lost vesting if termination occurs before the Scheduled Vesting Date unless expressly provided.
- Misconduct forfeiture: all RSUs (including any vested portion) are immediately forfeited upon a written determination of Misconduct; related Dividend Equivalents are forfeited or vest in tandem with the RSUs.
- RSU and share delivery: each RSU represents the right to receive one share upon vesting; no share distribution until vesting and settlement.
- Dividend Equivalents: credited for ordinary cash dividends declared after the Grant Date and before settlement/forfeiture; maintained in a non-interest-bearing bookkeeping account and vest/forfeit with the corresponding RSUs.
- Special vesting provisions: RSUs may continue to vest or vest on an accelerated basis in specified circumstances; Retirement treatment (for annual grants) allows continued vesting on schedule as if no termination, subject to potential acceleration and legal compliance caveats; references to possible “Qualifying Termination” provisions for special/retention grants.

Participants are responsible for compliance and should consult personal legal counsel.
- Section 409A: The Agreement is intended to comply with or be exempt from Section 409A; it will be interpreted accordingly. Each payment under the Agreement is a separate payment for 409A purposes.
- Appendix applicability: RSUs and Dividend Equivalents are subject to additional country-specific terms in the Appendix. If a participant resides in or relocates to a listed country, the Company may apply those terms for legal/administrative reasons. The Appendix forms part of the Agreement.
- Governing law and venue: Delaware law governs (excluding conflict-of-law rules requiring another jurisdiction’s laws). Disputes must be litigated exclusively in Minnesota (Ramsey County state courts or the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota).
- Appendix A terms/notifications: Provides extra country-specific conditions and informational notices (e.g., exchange controls), current as of December 1, 2022, and subject to change. Information is general, may not fit individual circumstances or relocations; participants should seek professional advice.
- Data privacy (EEA+): Participants in the EU/EEA/Switzerland/UK must review and accept the Data Privacy Notice and Declaration of Consent on the Company’s Fidelity platform as a condition of accepting the Agreement.
- Data privacy (outside EEA+): Participants consent to collection, use, and cross-border transfer of personal data by the Company, Employer, subsidiaries, and service providers (e.g., Fidelity) for plan administration. Data categories include identification, contact, employment, compensation, status, and equity details. Data may be processed in countries with different privacy laws (including the U.S.). nodes.summary:

- Securities law: Plan materials are not an advertisement or securities offering in Russia; shares are not registered in Russia and cannot be publicly circulated or delivered in Russia.
- Exchange controls: Temporary presidential decrees may bar Russian residents from receiving shares or sale proceeds into non-Russian bank/brokerage accounts (e.g., Fidelity). Rules change frequently; participants should consult legal advisors before accepting RSUs.
- Foreign asset/account reporting: Russian residents may need to file (1) annual reports by June 1 on cash flows and financial assets in offshore brokerage accounts, and one-time notifications within one month of (2) opening, (3) closing, or (4) changing details of such accounts. Consult a tax advisor.
- Anti-corruption: Certain public servants, their spouses, and dependent children are prohibited from owning foreign financial instruments; affected participants must inform the Company and should not hold shares acquired under the plan.
- Labor law: Continuing to hold shares after an involuntary termination may jeopardize eligibility for unemployment benefits in Russia.

nodes.summary:
- Overview: Country-specific terms, conditions, and legal notifications for participation in a Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) plan, covering labor law effects, tax/withholding, securities law status, data privacy, and exchange/control reporting in Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and Taiwan.

- Spain:
  - Labor law acknowledgment: RSUs are discretionary, not part of employment contract or salary/benefits; no indemnification if unvested RSUs are forfeited upon any termination (e.g., resignation, disciplinary dismissal, layoffs, relocations or material modifications under Spanish Worker’s Statute and related provisions).
  - Forfeiture: All unvested RSUs are automatically forfeited upon termination of service for any reason before vesting.
  - Discretionary nature: Grant is unilateral and conditional; rights can be null and void if assumptions/conditions are not met.
  - Securities law: RSUs do not qualify as securities; no public offer in Spain; not registered with the CNMV; no prospectus.
  - Exchange control: Possible obligation to declare foreign securities accounts and holdings to the Bank of Spain if annual transaction values or December 31 balances exceed thresholds; varying thresholds and deadlines; potential summarized filings.
  - Foreign asset/account reporting: Electronic declarations for foreign accounts, securities (including Plan shares), and transactions with non-residents when thresholds are exceeded; summarized reporting may apply below separate limits.

- Sweden:
  - Tax withholding: Company/Employer authorized to withhold or sell vested shares to cover tax-related items, irrespective of a formal obligation to withhold.

- Switzerland:
  - Securities law: Documents are not a FinSA prospectus; not for public distribution beyond employees; not filed with or approved by a Swiss reviewing body or FINMA.

- Taiwan:
  - Data privacy: Participants acknowledge and agree to data privacy terms for non-U.S./non-EEA; must execute required consents to participate.
  - Securities law: Offer limited to employees; not a public offer by a Taiwanese company.
  - Exchange control: Residents may remit foreign currency up to annual limits; larger single transactions may require a foreign exchange form and supporting documentation to the remitting bank.

- Sweden: Authorization for the company/employer to withhold or sell vested shares to cover tax-related items, supplementing the plan’s tax responsibility section.
- Switzerland: Securities law notices stating the materials are not a FinSA prospectus, cannot be publicly distributed beyond company employees, and are not filed with or approved by Swiss regulators (including FINMA).
- Taiwan: Data privacy requirements confirming participant consent and the need to execute any required privacy forms as a condition to participate.
- Taiwan: Securities law notice that the plan offer is only for employees and is not a public securities offering by a Taiwanese company.
- Taiwan: Exchange control guidance indicating residents can remit foreign currency up to annual limits and may need to file forms and provide documentation for larger single transactions.

nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines country-specific provisions for an employee equity plan (RSUs/Share-related awards):

- Thailand: Strict exchange control requirements. Proceeds from dividend equivalents, share sales, or dividends exceeding a set threshold per transaction must be immediately repatriated. Within 360 days of repatriation, funds must be converted to Thai Baht or placed in a foreign currency deposit account unless an exemption applies for offshore use with proper bank filings. Inward remittances must be reported to the Bank of Thailand via a foreign exchange transaction form. Non-compliance may trigger penalties. Participants should seek personal legal advice and are responsible for compliance.

- Trinidad and Tobago: No country-specific terms.

- Turkey: Securities cannot be sold in Turkey under local law; shares are listed on the NYSE (ticker MMM) and may be sold there. All foreign securities activities (e.g., selling shares) must be conducted through a bank or intermediary licensed by the Turkish Capital Markets Board and should be reported to the Board. Participants are responsible for compliance and should consult legal counsel.

- Ukraine: RSUs will be settled in cash (equal in value to the vested shares) rather than by issuing shares, despite any contrary plan terms, though the company reserves the right to settle in shares at its discretion.

- United Arab Emirates: The plan is a private offer limited to select employees as an incentive. It is not for distribution to or reliance by others. Prospective purchasers must conduct their own due diligence; those who do not understand the documents should consult an authorized financial adviser. The local regulator (ESCA) does not take responsibility for reviewing the offering.

nodes.summary:

- Thailand: Strict exchange control rules requiring immediate repatriation of proceeds above a threshold; within 360 days convert to Thai Baht or place in a foreign currency deposit account unless an exemption applies with proper documentation; mandatory reporting to the Bank of Thailand via a foreign exchange transaction form; penalties for non-compliance; participant bears responsibility and should seek legal advice.
- Trinidad and Tobago: No country-specific terms.
- Turkey: Participants may not sell Plan shares within Turkey; shares are traded on the NYSE (ticker “MMM”) and may be sold there; all foreign securities activities must be conducted through, and reported by, a bank/financial intermediary licensed by the Turkish Capital Markets Board; participant is responsible and should consult a legal advisor.
- Ukraine: RSUs will be settled in cash equal to the value of the vested shares; references to share issuance do not apply; company may, at its discretion, settle in shares.
- United Arab Emirates: Private, employee-only incentive offering; not for general distribution or reliance by others; participants should conduct their own due diligence and consult an authorized financial adviser; local regulators (ESCA, Ministry of Economy, Dubai DED) have not reviewed/approved and assume no responsibility for the documents.
- United Kingdom: Participants are liable for all tax-related items and must indemnify the company/employer for taxes paid or withheld; directors/executive officers may be unable to provide indemnification if deemed a loan, creating a taxable benefit requiring self-assessment reporting and payment of income tax and employee NICs; company/employer may recover amounts due.

nodes.summary:
- Regulatory disclaimer (UAE): States that neither the UAE Ministry of Economy nor the Dubai Department of Economic Development has approved, verified, or assumes responsibility for the Plan or Agreement.
- United Kingdom terms—Responsibility for Taxes: 
  - Participant is liable for all tax-related items and must pay amounts requested by the Company, Employer, or HMRC (or other authorities).
  - Participant agrees to indemnify the Company and Employer for any taxes they pay or withhold on the participant’s behalf.
  - For directors/executive officers (per Exchange Act Section 13(k)), indemnification may be treated as a prohibited loan; in such cases, uncollected taxes may be a taxable benefit subject to income tax and NICs.
  - Participant must report and pay any such tax under self-assessment and pay employee NICs to the Company/Employer, recoverable as outlined in Section 2.1.
- Vietnam terms—Cash settlement of RSUs:
  - Vested RSUs will be settled in cash equal to the value of the shares; references to share issuance do not apply.
  - The Company reserves discretion to settle RSUs in shares instead.
